title: Factory hardening: guard, allow list, tests, docs
request: Close the open factory follow-ups after the plan review: fail-closed guard, backslash-newline and escaped-quote gaps, combined push flags, Bash writes to control-plane files ask the human, tighter allow list, fake key in a spec, a weak CLI test, two PIPELINE.md notes. Plan: scratchpad PLAN-factory-follow-ups.md (v2).

criteria.text: No factory source file matches the guard's own secret pattern: the fake key in guard.spec.mjs is built from pieces, and a new test proves it for every file under factory/spec, factory/hooks and factory/bin
criteria.evidence: DONE. Test: no factory source file holds a whole credential, so the guard lets the factory write its own files (guard.spec). The fake key in the spec is built from pieces. Passing in factory-specs (97/97) at 705428f.

criteria.text: The guard fails closed: any internal error, unparsable or empty input, or a failed git read during the secret scan blocks Bash commands (exit 2); the hook command in .claude/settings.json and the template ends with an exit-2 fallback so load-time failures (missing file, syntax error) also block; Edit and Write fall back to the built-in blocks and then ask on every other edit; built-in protected paths are always merged into a weak or empty config (spawn tests)
criteria.evidence: DONE. Tests in guard.spec: a config that cannot be read (Bash exits 2, every edit asks, env file stays blocked); a valid but weak config cannot switch built-in protection off; hardenConfig; unparsable or empty input exits 2; a git failure while scanning a commit exits 2; a repo with no commit yet; the hook command in both settings files fails closed. All pass at 705428f.

criteria.text: A backslash plus newline cannot hide a command, using an odd-run-aware join that keeps an even run of backslashes as it is today: split-word push-to-main and protected-path-delete examples are blocked and the existing even-run case stays blocked
criteria.evidence: DONE for the stated examples. Tests: backslash-newline inside a word cannot hide a push to the protected branch or a protected path; an even run of backslashes stays its own command; the guard checks the written text AND the joined text; a block in either text wins; an ask that shows only after the join is kept (mutation-proven). KNOWN GAP, written in the README and also present in the base commit 6fc7d70: a comment that ends in a backslash PLUS a split word on a later line is not seen in either text. Not fixed here.

criteria.text: Backslash-escaped quotes and dollar-single-quote strings no longer hide commands, in both the main quote scanner and the substitution scanner; no existing test changed; the replacer cannot crash on an escape pair
criteria.evidence: DONE for the stated cases. Tests: an escaped quote does not open a quoted string that hides a command; substitution found after an escaped quote, an ANSI-C quote or an apostrophe in double quotes; a closing paren inside quotes does not end a substitution early; escape handling keeps the allowed and already-blocked forms. No existing assertion changed. KNOWN GAP, in the README and also in base: a nested quote holding an apostrophe inside a substitution can hide a later substitution. Not fixed here.

criteria.text: git push with combined short flags that contain f and plus-prefixed refspecs are blocked; -u, --follow-tags, --set-upstream, -o, --force-with-lease and a push followed by an unrelated command stay allowed
criteria.evidence: DONE. Tests: every push in a command is checked, quoted names and bare HEAD included; quote marks inside a branch name do not hide a push to a protected branch; a force flag cannot hide in a short flag group or a plus-prefixed ref; the force-flag check stays fast on a very long flag word; safe push forms stay allowed. All pass at 705428f.

criteria.text: Bash writes to control-plane files ask the human (redirects; tee, cp, install, ln, rsync, mv, rm and similar by the right argument; sed -i; dd of=; curl -o; git checkout or restore from a ref; git apply, patch, am; an anchored python/node/bash -c or -e with a literal path); reads, git add, git commit with a heredoc that mentions a control file, node --test and branch switches stay silent (negative tests); a block always wins over an ask; one spawn test sees permissionDecision ask; a manual smoke result is recorded
criteria.evidence: PARTIAL. Automated part DONE: part A and part B tests (redirects, tee, cp, mv, sed -i, dd, curl, git checkout from a ref, git apply, patch, anchored one-liners; negative tests for reads and look-alikes; a block always wins; the real hook returns an ask in a spawn test). The manual smoke is NOT done: I cannot see permission prompts from this session. UNKNOWN: whether a hook ask beats an allow rule, and whether Auto mode answers a hook ask. Needs a human observation.

criteria.text: The npm, node and playwright allow rules are tightened to explicit names in .claude/settings.json and the template; the installer derives allow rules from the target's verify checks and preview command, never adds a blanket npm run rule, warns if one exists, and never deletes user rules; a settings test proves every verify check and the preview command of this repo still matches an allow rule
criteria.evidence: DONE. Allow list uses explicit names (the blanket npm run rule is gone; the grep rule was removed after review). settings.spec proves every verify check and the preview command still match an allow rule and that no blanket rule exists. install.spec proves the installer derives rules from the target checks, never adds a blanket rule, warns when one exists, adds no duplicates and never deletes user rules.

criteria.text: cli.spec asserts READY (exit 0) and NOT READY (exit 1) explicitly; changing APPROVE to CHANGES in the setup, and dropping the commit in the setup, both pass the old test and fail the new one (mutation proof, run and shown)
criteria.evidence: PARTIAL. The gate test now asserts the exit status and the words READY and NOT READY. Mutation 1 (change APPROVE to CHANGES in the setup) passes the old test and fails the new one: shown. Mutation 2 (drop the commit in the setup) is an equivalent mutant: the gate reads the last commit that touches non-bookkeeping paths, so it changes nothing the gate reads and fails neither test. Only one of the two named mutations is proven.

criteria.text: PIPELINE.md Stage 1 branch order (new, then switch, then set branch) and the --trivial rule are corrected in PIPELINE.md, the factory-maintain skill and the README; the README Known limits state honestly what shell-write matching covers and what it does not, and the stale cd and tested-by notes are fixed
criteria.evidence: DONE with notes. The branch order and the trivial rule are corrected in PIPELINE.md, the factory-maintain skill and the README; Known limits lists what is covered, what asks and what is not covered; stale notes fixed. The independent review found three README sentences that are slightly too strong or too narrow (the quoted-heredoc form needs a second closing line; the nested-quote gap also holds for a single-quoted word with a double-quote mark; deep-nest timings differ by machine). Not yet fixed; carried to a follow-up.

criteria.text: The guard specs run as a non-required check named factory-specs and pass after every commit; all factory specs pass; the repo checks pass (integrity, typecheck, lint, knip, build, unit); no existing assertion weakened; any assertion that must change is listed in the report
criteria.evidence: DONE. factory-specs is a non-required check and passes (97/97) at 705428f. All six repo checks pass at 705428f: integrity, typecheck, lint, knip, build, unit. No assertion weakened or removed. Changes to existing tests, listed: (a) the cli.spec assertion for an unconfigured check name was inverted on purpose (human decision: refuse the double-dash override); (b) the gate test was strengthened; (c) one guard test was retitled, body unchanged.

criteria.text: The check command refuses a '-- <cmd>' override for a name that is not configured and for a required check, and runs nothing. A configured check that is not required still accepts it (a known gap, written in the README). Shown by the CLI spec.
criteria.evidence: DONE. cli.spec: a required check and an unconfigured name both refuse a substitute command; a refused override runs nothing and leaves no trace; a configured check that is not required still accepts it (the known gap, in the README); names that exist only on Object.prototype never count as configured. KNOWN GAP: check with such a name and NO override crashes with a TypeError stack trace (no command runs, task file unchanged); documented, not fixed.

reviews.summary: Round 2 at b534e5c: B1, B2, N2, N5 closed with exit-2 proof; 0 regressions vs base in ~50k real-bash fuzz cases; 94/94 specs, no assertion removed. Open notes (none are regressions): mixed join (comment or quoted heredoc plus split word) still hides a command in both texts and in base; nested-quote substitution; nested $( ) speed back to base level; ask-from-joined-text untested.

Delta 537d9a1/bb05a9b/705428f at 705428f: firstVisit keyed on depth plus body is correct (180k decisions identical to pre-delta; body-only key loses coverage in 49 of 60k), N-a test is a real pin, 97/97 specs, no assertion removed. Open notes: nest of ~750+ deep exceeds the 20 s hook timeout (cubic); two README sentences too narrow or too strong; key choice and control-scan dedupe not pinned by tests.

history.summary: The backslash-newline join hides a command after a comment that ends in a backslash and after a quoted heredoc body. Fix: check the raw text and the joined text, a block wins.
The substitution body skip loses the quote state when a closing paren sits inside quotes. Fix: remove the skip.

notes.text: Plan v2 in scratchpad/PLAN-factory-follow-ups.md after an independent PLAN review (CHANGES accepted). Exact attack strings live only in spec files because the guard blocks quoted prose that contains them. Open decisions for Doug: refuse the check double-dash override unless the check is configured (recommend yes); CODEOWNERS (recommend not now: a sole owner deadlocks own PRs). Edits to factory/**, .claude/settings.json and .factory/config.json ask the human.
